props.gloss_en: one may open [a channel of] water to a garden on Shabbat eve at nightfall, and it goes on filling all day
one may place incense under the garments and sulfur under the vessels on Shabbat eve, and they go on being perfumed / sulfured all Shabbat
one may place eye-salve on the eye and a bandage on a wound on Shabbat eve at nightfall, and it goes on healing all day
but one may not put wheat into a water-mill unless it will be ground while it is still day
Rabba: [the mill is forbidden] because it makes a noise
Rav Yosef: [the mill is forbidden] because of the resting of vessels
'and in all that I have said to you take heed' (Ex 23:13) -- to include the resting of vessels
now that you said Beit Hillel hold that the resting of vessels is Torah law
Beit Hillel permit putting bundles of flax into the oven [at nightfall]
Beit Hillel permit putting wool into the dyer's kettle [at nightfall]
Beit Hillel permit spreading traps for beast, bird and fish [at nightfall]
who is the tanna who holds the resting of vessels is Torah law? Beit Shammai, and not Beit Hillel
for Beit Shammai, whether [the vessel] performs an act or does not, it is forbidden
for Beit Hillel, even though [the vessel] performs an act, it is permitted
a woman may not fill a pot with groats and lupines and put it into the oven on Shabbat eve at nightfall; if she did, at the end of Shabbat they are forbidden for as long as it takes to make them
likewise a baker may not fill a barrel of water and put it into the oven on Shabbat eve at nightfall; if he did, it is forbidden at the end of Shabbat for as long as it takes to make it
(entertained) shall we say this tosefta is Beit Shammai's and not Beit Hillel's?
even if you say [it is] Beit Hillel's: [it is] a decree lest he stoke the coals
since wind harms them, he does not uncover [the oven] -- [so he will not come to stoke]
Shmuel: [the mishnah's wool-into-the-kettle is] in a kettle removed [from the fire]
in [a kettle] removed and sealed [with plaster]
a pot of raw [meat] may be put into the oven on Shabbat eve at nightfall
why? since it is not fit for the evening, he puts it out of his mind and will not come to stoke the coals
and [a pot of] cooked [food] -- it is fine
cooked and not [fully] cooked -- forbidden
and if he threw a raw bone into it -- it is fine
kid's meat [in an oven] sealed [with clay] -- it is fine
ram's meat [in an oven] not sealed -- forbidden
kid's meat, oven not sealed -- permitted
kid's meat, oven not sealed -- forbidden
ram's meat, oven sealed -- permitted
ram's meat, oven sealed -- forbidden
(איכא דאמרי) ram's meat, oven not sealed -- permitted
one does not roast meat, an onion or an egg [on Shabbat eve] unless they can be roasted while it is still day
Ravina: a raw gourd -- it is fine [to put in at nightfall]
Ravina: since wind harms it, it is like kid's meat
